purpose: Challenge an exact UTF-8 string-Anum transport over the same four abits without changing recursive Anum grammar or equating source glyphs with semantic root meanings.

candidateA.name: binary-byte-envelope
candidateA.reason: begin/end abits remain explicit byte-context boundaries while 0/1 carry binary byte payload

candidateB.name: two-bit-quaternary-digits
candidateB.concern: [ and ] become ordinary digit values inside a byte and byte boundary is supplied only by external fixed width rather than their root begin/end reading

sourceSemanticBoundary.example: the source glyph '[' is UTF-8 byte 0x5B encoded as [01011011], not the same occurrence as the root begin abit used to delimit that byte

requiredAssertions: all 256 byte values round-trip through candidate A
candidate A byte carriers have exact [ + 8 binary payload + ] shape
malformed byte carriers reject wrong width, boundaries and non-binary payload
concatenated byte carriers round-trip arbitrary byte sequences
representative ASCII, Cyrillic, formal MTS glyphs, combining text and emoji round-trip exact UTF-8 bytes and text
invalid UTF-8 bytes round-trip at byte layer but strict text decoding rejects them
NFC and decomposed source spellings remain byte-distinct when caller supplied them distinctly
literal source glyphs 0 1 [ ] bootstrap through the same byte protocol without host exceptions
[01000001] decodes as byte A under byte protocol and remains RAW under accepted recursive-root denotation
source glyph [ encodes to [01011011] and is not identical to the delimiter abit occurrence
candidate B also byte-round-trips but does not preserve explicit begin/end positions inside each byte carrier
no production context enum or recursive grammar is modified
notDecided: candidate A acceptance as the canonical string-Anum transport
whether byte envelope boundaries are semantic context transitions or only transport framing
how byte carriers compose into a semantic string-link network
the exact dictionary relation from string Anum to formal sign/form
whether the full interpreter consumes bytes, decoded Unicode code points or dictionary tokens
